proposed.explanation:
Annualised 2026 EPS and P/E

The only verified earnings figure in the report is the 9-month EPS: 8.74 EGP for the nine months to 30 Sep 2026 (up 104 % from 4.28 EGP in the same period a year earlier). A simple annualisation (× 12/9) gives an estimated full-year 2026 EPS of ≈ 11.65 EGP. At the current price of 76.21 EGP the implied P/E is roughly 6.5×, which is low by most standards and suggests the market is not fully pricing in the earnings recovery.

Why I am still cautious
• The annualisation is a rough proxy. The FY-2025 EPS column (≈ 1.99 EGP) is well below the 9M-2025 EPS of 4.28 EGP, implying a Q4-2025 loss of about 2.3 EGP per share. If Q4-2026 repeats that pattern, true full-year EPS could be materially lower than 11.65, pushing the P/E higher.
• The revenue and net-profit rows on the same page carry an AMBIGUOUS unit tag (the page mixes 'مليار' and 'مليون' headers), so I cannot independently verify the top-line or bottom-line trends. This limits my confidence in the sustainability of the EPS jump.
• No dividend data is provided, so the 'income' leg of your goal cannot be assessed from this evidence alone.

Position sizing and diversification
You hold 30,000 EGP in cash and no other positions. The 50 % single-stock cap means I can allocate at most 15,000 EGP to ABUK. At 76.21 EGP that is 196 shares (cost 14,937.16 EGP), leaving 15,062.84 EGP in cash. ABUK would represent ≈ 49.8 % of the total portfolio value, just under the limit. Buying 197 shares would push the weight to 50.04 %, which is not permitted.

Fit with your profile
A 3–5 year horizon and medium risk tolerance are compatible with a low-P/E exporter that is showing strong earnings momentum. The cash buffer (≈ 50 % of the portfolio) provides a cushion if Q4 disappoints or if you want to add to the position later. This is guidance, not a guarantee: the annualised P/E could shift significantly once the full-year results are published, and the ambiguous revenue/profit figures mean I cannot rule out a one-off or non-recurring driver behind the 104 % EPS growth.
limitations: Full-year 2026 EPS is an annualised estimate (9M × 4/3), not an actual reported figure; Q4 seasonality or one-off items could change it materially.
Revenue and net-profit rows are AMBIGUOUS (mixed unit headers on the page), so top-line and bottom-line trends cannot be independently verified.
No dividend or payout-ratio data is available to assess the income component of the investor's goal.
The FY-2025 EPS column (≈ 1.99 EGP) being below the 9M-2025 EPS (4.28 EGP) implies a Q4-2025 loss, which raises uncertainty about Q4-2026.
